definitions.explanation: Food that has not been cooked thoroughly, leaving the inside raw or partially raw. Can also be used figuratively to describe something incomplete or half-done.

examples.japanese: この{肉|にく}は{生焼|なまや}けだ。
{生焼|なまや}けの{鶏肉|とりにく}は{食中毒|しょくちゅうどく}の{原因|げんいん}になる。
examples.english: Undercooked chicken can cause food poisoning.

examples.japanese: ハンバーグの{中|なか}がまだ{生焼|なまや}けだったので、もう{少|すこ}し{焼|や}くことにした。
examples.english: The inside of the hamburger steak was still undercooked, so I decided to cook it a bit more.

notes:
Composed of {生|なま} (raw) and {焼|や}け (burning/cooking). Describes food that appears cooked on the outside but remains raw or insufficiently cooked on the inside. This is an important concept in food safety, especially with meats.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生焼|なまや}けの{肉|にく}: undercooked meat
- {生焼|なまや}け{状態|じょうたい}: undercooked state
- {中|なか}が{生焼|なまや}け: undercooked inside

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生|なま}: raw — completely uncooked
- レア: rare (cooking term) — borrowed from English; intentionally served lightly cooked
- {焼|や}きすぎ: overcooked — too much cooking, the opposite problem
- {半生|はんなま}: half-raw / semi-dried — can mean partially raw food or half-dried products like noodles
